- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 65), model tends to overshoot; cap next 3 days’ forecast at +3% above peak.  
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.4) and forecast is below recent 5-day average, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.  
- Model often underestimates late-period rallies (last 5–7 days of forecast); add 1–3% buffer if sentiment >0.3.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: shift forecast toward 30-day moving average.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating ±0.25), reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting noise.
